title: A Real Hovorka Model, Not a Generic Diabetes Game | vitalii.no
description:
Why a type 1 diabetes simulator for one real kid had to throw out every generic body model and run the actual math his doctor uses.

Artem's parents wanted him to understand his diabetes by playing, not by reading a textbook. But every public insulin simulator online runs on a generic body, so none of the carb ratios, correction doses or night lows it taught him matched what his own doctor had actually calibrated for him. The lesson was useless, or worse, misleading.

The fix was to stop simulating a generic patient and simulate Artem. js/t1d-model.js implements the Hovorka 2004 differential-equation model per kilogram of his own body weight, with NovoRapid and Levemir absorption curves, ketone accumulation, delayed glucose rise from fat and protein, exercise effects that carry into the night, and the dawn phenomenon. js/day.js wraps it in a 24-hour day with meal reminders, a NovoRapid correction-dose calculator, and four missions built around his real routine — a forgotten Levemir dose, pizza night, football practice, the night after.

The correction-dose math and glucose curves now match the values on sheet 08.10, Artem's own doctor's worksheet, instead of a generic textbook body. His parents can update his IKF, Levemir dose and weight under 'My values' as he grows, with no code changes needed.
